kernel_adaptation_genuineness.claim_matc.reason: The stated far-field kernel uses raw occurrence-sum features with one amplitude per family. The implemented full-scale kernel divides each motif feature by its own training RMS. These unequal within-family factors change the covariance and cannot be absorbed into the shared family amplitude.
evidence: proposal/sections/methodology.tex:73-88 explicitly defines phi as the unnormalized occurrence sum and beta as a family amplitude; sections/setup.tex:45-46 specifies R0=1.
proposal/code/motif_gp.py:74-84 divides Phi by per-column RMS; lines 178-188 apply the same normalization to evaluation features; lines 339-346 use those features with family-shared beta.

Read-only recount of proposal/data/seq_train.txt, using the full model_config.json motif/family assignments: family-0 motifs CGCGCG and CACCCC have squared-count sums 8,504 and 29,583 over 500,000 rows. Their normalization therefore multiplies covariance contributions by 58.7959 and 16.9016, respectively.

code_paper_alignment.methodology_describ.reason: The mathematical description materially contradicts the implemented feature weighting. With family-shared amplitudes, per-motif RMS normalization changes relative covariance contributions within each family. This is a different kernel specification, rather than an equivalent computation or merely missing implementation detail.

The full model_config.json assigns CGCGCG and CACCCC to family 0. Recounting saved training sequences gives RMS values 0.1304147231 and 0.2432406216, producing approximately a 3.48-fold difference in relative kernel weighting that a single family amplitude cannot remove.
